comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The current University of Twente curriculum page explicitly identifies its course-code and study-unit table as 2026-2027, defines four coherent 15-EC modules in each of years one and two, and gives year three as a 30-EC minor followed by 15 EC of thesis preparation and a 15-EC BSc thesis. The first year covers the construction, water, and traffic domains; the second year integrates delta safety, sustainable civil engineering, area development, and simulation and stochastic modelling. The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without inventing a choice. Every listed study unit and the minor account for exactly 180 EC. Fixed-queue review on 2026-10-16 rechecked the current 2026-27 curriculum and programme description. All settled components, EC and the neutral route decision are preserved. Related UCR programmes address environmental assessment and the ecological/social impacts of infrastructure without claiming civil-engineering design training.
components: Introduction to Programming in Engineering using Python 1
Introduction to Programming in Engineering using Python 2
Energy Use in the Built Environment
Simulation and Stochastic Modelling in Civil Engineering Project
Genuine open minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

core: Infrastructure, construction, water and transport design with engineering mathematics and domain projects
Water management, flood risk and resilient deltas
Environmental assessment, circular materials and sustainable infrastructure
Stakeholder interests, social sustainability and the wider effects of infrastructure
Quantitative modelling, simulation and research for environmental decisions
adjacent: Environmental geoscience and quantitative assessment of water and delta risks
Ecological, resource and social consequences of sustainable infrastructure
questions: How can delta communities manage flooding, freshwater, subsidence and environmental impacts?
How can circular resource use, nature-based solutions and public participation improve infrastructure decisions?

candidates.label: Infrastructure sustainability, ecological impacts and governance

alternatives.label: Water, delta risks & quantitative environmental science
alternatives.labelReason: Sixteen environmental, water, resource and sustainability courses and seven mathematical/computational courses define the curriculum. Water and delta risk provide the application; quantitative environmental assessment is substantial. No structural, hydraulic or transport-engineering sequence is implied.
alternatives.concept: Investigate water and delta risks through environmental geoscience, water governance, circular resource assessment and quantitative modelling. The programme combines field/GIS and geochemical tools with calculus, probability, numerical methods and data processing. It is a related environmental-science response to Civil Engineering, with engineering design, structures, hydraulics and transport remaining outside its coverage.
progression: Environmental and mathematical gateways precede dependent advanced study. Dynamic Earth and Building with Nature precede the water, GIS and aquifer courses; Python and Mathematical Methods precede numerical methods; linear algebra precedes numerical methods and advanced calculus. The sustainability material-science gateway precedes recovery/remediation and resource research. Exact planned terms and all formal prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Sustainable infrastructure: ecology, resources & governance
alternatives.labelReason: Nineteen environmental, ecology, water and resource courses form the core. Four sociology, research-method and communication courses address the evidenced social impacts and public choices around infrastructure, plus mandatory PPD. The label identifies infrastructure as the application of an environmental programme and does not imply civil-engineering design training.
alternatives.concept: Assess how infrastructure decisions affect coastal ecosystems, water, resources and communities, combining nature-based solutions, environmental field methods, circular resource and energy assessment, governance, environmental justice and stakeholder research. This is a related sustainability programme rather than construction or transport engineering.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses / 60 EC differ in each direction. The second programme replaces seven mathematics/computing courses and Earth System Science Tools with biodiversity, ecosystems, marine ecology, renewable-system assessment, sociology, qualitative stakeholder inquiry, environmental justice and climate communication. This materially shifts the programme from quantitative environmental analysis to ecological consequences and collective infrastructure decisions.
progression: Biodiversity and ecosystem foundations precede marine ecology. Environmental gateways precede geochemical, material-recovery and renewable-energy assessment. Building with Nature and Dynamic Earth precede advanced water and field methods. Qualitative methods precede the regional research project. Every exact planned term and formal prerequisite is checked.

selection.assessment: Two complete related programmes are included sequentially. A third traffic/transport direction cannot sustain a complete target-linked programme: mathematics, Python, numerical analysis and probability can supply general modelling methods, but the catalogue lacks traffic-flow theory, transport demand, network/transport policy and transport-design project sequences. Robotics path planning is autonomous motion planning, not traffic engineering, and algorithm courses alone would change the concept to computing. Construction concerns are covered only through material sustainability, nature-based solutions and impacts in ucr-2; no structural, geotechnical, fluid-mechanics or construction-design substitute is claimed.

trace: introduces planetary boundaries and environmental thresholds used to evaluate the sustainability of water and infrastructure interventions
introduces geology, geomorphology, sedimentology, geohydrology and field observation relevant to water, flood and subsidence assessment
directly examines nature-based construction and coastal protection in Zeeland, including habitat impacts and the use of natural processes; it is not structural engineering
directly teaches Python programming, testing and computational problem-solving as the coding foundation for numerical environmental analysis
teaches chemistry and material science for sustainability, supplying the formal and substantive foundation for resource recovery and renewable-system assessment
directly teaches differentiation, integration and differential equations needed to formulate quantitative environmental change and flow models
teaches earth-system modelling, proxies and tracers linking water, land, atmosphere and climate, a specific method for environmental-impact assessment
directly teaches matrices, linear equations, eigenvalues and transformations for multivariable environmental models and geospatial/data analysis
directly teaches probability distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation for environmental uncertainty and risk analysis; it is not traffic-flow modelling
directly evaluates product and process impacts from extraction to disposal or reuse, providing lifecycle and circularity methods for material/resource decisions
directly examines soil-mineral-water interactions, nutrient and metal leaching, wastewater treatment and resource recovery using geochemical modelling
directly studies flood protection, drainage, salinisation, freshwater, subsidence and the ecological/social consequences of water infrastructure and governance
directly teaches GIS, remotely sensed data integration and earth-science case analysis for soil/water governance and coastal-protection planning
directly investigates soil properties, remediation and aquifer mapping through field/laboratory work for freshwater, coastal protection and geothermal assessment; it is not soil mechanics
directly teaches numerical root finding, interpolation, integration and differential-equation algorithms, including sensitivity and interpretation of computational results
studies sea-level rise, climate feedbacks and impacts on construction and transport, then examines mitigation and adaptation including climate-resilient planning
directly examines resource stewardship, recovery and remediation technologies with inorganic chemistry and laboratory skills for evaluating circular resource use, not construction-material strength
conducts partner-defined sustainability research in the Zeeland delta, applying environmental or stakeholder methods to a regional problem; a specific infrastructure project is not guaranteed
directly teaches cleaning, manipulation and visualisation of tabular and spatial data with a research project, providing the workflow for analysing environmental observations
teaches geoscientific risk analysis and adaptation for floods, droughts and other hazards, complementing delta resilience without engineering safety design
researches geothermal energy, waste storage and carbon capture through literature review and professional reporting, assessing environmental consequences of resource interventions
analyses rule-making, actor interests and policy enforcement and applies governance concepts to freshwater, energy and climate decisions
extends calculus to multivariable functions and differential equations with computer algebra, providing specific mathematical tools for environmental-system models
introduces biodiversity, ecological roles and investigation methods needed to assess habitat consequences of nature-based infrastructure
directly examines interactions between organisms and their chemical/physical surroundings, ecological modelling and applied cases for evaluating ecosystem responses to intervention
analyses how climate claims and competing responses are communicated through texts and public media, providing a specific method for evaluating public debate around adaptation
introduces social institutions, inequality and sociological inquiry, supplying the foundation for investigating how infrastructure choices affect different communities
directly teaches qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity for investigating affected communities and stakeholder meanings
directly studies coastal and estuarine ecosystems and the impacts of human activities on them, providing specific assessment of infrastructure effects at the land-sea boundary

directly assesses energy-use patterns and renewable options through technical/economic analysis and a partner-company report; it supports sustainable energy decisions without replacing building-services engineering
directly examines environmental justice and contested environmental projects through social-movement theory and Environmental Justice Atlas cases

notes.text: Twente combines structures, hydraulics, soil mechanics, transport and construction design with integrated civil-engineering projects. These UCR programmes address water and delta risks, environmental assessment and infrastructure impacts through geoscience, quantitative methods, ecology, resources and governance. They do not provide the structural, geotechnical, hydraulic, traffic or construction-engineering sequence.
